CWE-351.name: Insufficient Type Distinction
CWE-351.question: Does this function treat values of different kinds as interchangeable, so that one kind can be passed off as another to reach a security decision?

any: a check accepts a value without testing its kind, for example an array, object or number where a string identifier was expected
different message or record types are told apart only by a field the sender controls, and are then handled with the same authority
a parameter that may be a single item or a list is used in a check that behaves differently for each, such as membership versus equality
the function tests the value's type or tag explicitly and rejects unexpected kinds before the check
the type is fixed by a static type system or a strict schema that has already been applied in this function
the values are only displayed or logged, with no security effect

distinguish_from.CWE-1287: the problem is simply not checking that input has the expected type, without one kind impersonating another

CWE-352.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
CWE-352.question: Does this request handler change state on behalf of a cookie-authenticated user without checking an anti-forgery token or equivalent?

any: a POST, PUT, DELETE or state-changing GET handler that relies on the session cookie performs an update with no CSRF token comparison
CSRF protection is explicitly turned off for the handler, for example with an exempt decorator or by skipping the middleware
a token is read but compared incorrectly, for example only when present, or against a value the attacker can also supply
the handler or its framework decorator verifies a per-session CSRF token before acting
authentication uses a header the browser does not send automatically, such as a bearer token, rather than a cookie
the handler only reads data and changes no state

distinguish_from.CWE-1385: the endpoint is a WebSocket upgrade accepted without an Origin check

CWE-353.name: Missing Support for Integrity Check
CWE-353.question: Does this function send or accept data over a channel or format with no checksum, hash or MAC that would reveal corruption or tampering?

any: a message, packet, file or record format is built or parsed with no integrity field at all
the function encrypts data with a mode that has no authentication, such as CBC or CTR without a separate MAC
a protocol frame is assembled and transmitted where neither side can detect altered bytes
the format includes a checksum, CRC, hash, MAC or signature that the function computes or checks
the data travels over a channel that provides integrity, such as TLS, or uses authenticated encryption like AES-GCM
the data is transient and internal, never leaving the process

distinguish_from.CWE-354: an integrity value exists in the format but the function does not check it, or checks it wrongly

CWE-354.name: Improper Validation of Integrity Check Value
CWE-354.question: Does this function receive data with a checksum, hash or MAC but skip that check, compare it wrongly, or carry on when it fails?

any: a received checksum or MAC field is parsed but never compared with a value computed from the data
the comparison result is ignored, logged only, or a mismatch still lets processing continue
the value is compared over only part of the data, or with the wrong length or byte order
the integrity value is recomputed over the whole payload and a mismatch rejects the data on every path
the format carries no integrity value at all, which is a different weakness
the function only computes integrity values for outgoing data

distinguish_from.CWE-353: the format has no integrity value at all
distinguish_from.CWE-347: the value being checked is a public-key signature

CWE-357.name: Insufficient UI Warning of Dangerous Operations
CWE-357.question: Does this function carry out a destructive, irreversible or security-weakening action requested from the user interface without warning the user or asking for confirmation?

any: a UI event handler deletes data, overwrites files, sends payments or disables protection immediately with no confirmation step
a dialog that should warn about a dangerous action is skipped, shown with misleading wording, or defaults to the dangerous choice
opening an untrusted file or link from the interface runs content without any prompt
the action is preceded by an explicit confirmation or a clear warning that names the consequence
the action is easily undone, such as moving an item to a recycle bin
the function has no user-facing trigger, such as a batch job or internal helper

distinguish_from.CWE-450: the user's input could mean two different things and the code silently picks one

CWE-360.name: Trust of System Event Data
CWE-360.question: Does this function act on a system or window event, signal or message as if it must have come from a trusted source, without checking the sender?

any: a handler for window messages, broadcast intents, signals or inter-process events performs a privileged action based solely on receiving the event
a browser message event handler uses event.data without checking event.origin or event.source
the event carries parameters such as a callback address or command that are used directly
the handler verifies the sender, for example comparing event.origin to an expected value or checking the sending process credentials
the event only triggers a harmless refresh with no data taken from it
the event source is created within the same function and cannot be reached by other parties

CWE-450.name: Multiple Interpretations of UI Input
CWE-450.question: Does this function take user input that could mean two different things and silently act on one meaning, possibly the less safe one?

any: an input string is tried first as one kind of target, such as a command or URL, and otherwise as another, such as a file path or search term
a name that matches both a local item and a remote or privileged item is resolved without telling the user which was chosen
an input is parsed loosely so that different formats, such as a date or number in two locales, are accepted with no indication of which reading was used
the function requires the input type to be stated explicitly, such as a prefix, separate field or flag
an ambiguous input is rejected or the user is asked to choose
only one interpretation is possible for the accepted input format

distinguish_from.CWE-357: the input is unambiguous but a dangerous action proceeds without warning

CWE-494.name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
CWE-494.question: Does this function download code, a plugin, script or update and run or install it without checking a signature or known hash?

any: content fetched over a network is written to disk and then executed, loaded as a library or imported
a remote script is piped into an interpreter or passed to eval after download
an update or package is installed from a URL with no hash comparison or signature verification before use
the downloaded file's hash or signature is checked against a pinned value before it is run, and failure aborts
the downloaded content is data that is parsed, not executed
the code is loaded from a local, read-only location rather than fetched

distinguish_from.CWE-347: a signature check exists but is performed incorrectly

CWE-526.name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in an Environment Variable
CWE-526.question: Does this function place a password, key or other secret unencrypted into an environment variable, or expose environment variables holding secrets?

any: a secret is assigned to an environment variable for the current or a child process
c: setenv, putenv or an envp array for exec includes a password or key
javascript: process.env.X = secret, or a child_process env object containing a secret
python: os.environ[...] = secret, os.putenv, or a subprocess env dict containing a secret
rust: std::env::set_var or Command::env passes a secret

any: the function only reads configuration from the environment and does not set or reveal it
secrets are passed through a file descriptor, protected file or secret manager instead
the variable holds non-sensitive configuration

distinguish_from.CWE-312: the secret is stored in some other place, such as a file or database

CWE-602.name: Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security
CWE-602.question: Does this function rely on checks done in client-side code for a rule that the server must enforce?

any: a server handler trusts a field computed or validated by the client, such as a price, total, role, isAdmin flag or validated marker
access control or input validation exists only in browser or mobile code, for example hiding a button or disabling a field, and the matching server path does not repeat it
a server endpoint skips validation because a comment or flag says the client already did it
the server handler independently re-checks permissions and validates input before acting
the client-side check is only for user convenience and the server code path it calls also enforces the rule
the function runs entirely on a trusted server with no client involvement

distinguish_from.CWE-807: a server-side security decision reads an untrusted cookie, header or parameter rather than relying on client logic
distinguish_from.CWE-862: the server handler simply has no authorisation check at all

CWE-614.name: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
CWE-614.question: Does this function set a session or other sensitive cookie without the Secure attribute?

any: a Set-Cookie header for a session, auth or CSRF cookie lacks the Secure flag
javascript: res.cookie or a cookie options object for a sensitive cookie sets secure: false or omits secure
python: set_cookie for a session or auth cookie without secure=True, or SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE set to False
rust: a cookie builder for an auth cookie without .secure(true)

any: the Secure flag is set on the cookie
the cookie is non-sensitive, such as a display preference
the framework default visible in the function enforces Secure

distinguish_from.CWE-315: the cookie's value itself exposes sensitive data in readable form

CWE-646.name: Reliance on File Name or Extension of Externally-Supplied File
CWE-646.question: Does this function decide how to treat an uploaded or external file only from its name, extension or declared content type?

any: an upload is accepted or rejected by checking the filename's extension, for example endswith('.jpg')
the client-supplied Content-Type or MIME field decides whether a file is safe or how it is processed
the extension picks a handler or interpreter for the file contents
the function inspects the file contents, such as magic bytes or a full parse with a strict decoder, before trusting it
the file is stored under a server-generated name in a non-executable location and served as a download
the extension is used only to label or display the file

distinguish_from.CWE-434: dangerous file types can be uploaded with no type check at all

CWE-649.name: Reliance on Obfuscation or Encryption of Security-Relevant Inputs without Integrity Checking
CWE-649.question: Does this function trust a value it gets back from the client, such as an encrypted or encoded cookie or hidden field, because it is encrypted, without checking integrity?

any: a value round-tripped through the client is decrypted and used for a security decision with no MAC or signature check
data is encrypted with an unauthenticated mode, or merely encoded, and decrypting without error is taken as proof it is genuine
a role, price or user id is recovered from an obfuscated parameter and trusted
the value is protected with authenticated encryption or a MAC that is verified before use
the security relevant value is kept on the server and the client holds only an opaque random session key
the decoded value is treated as untrusted input and validated like any other

distinguish_from.CWE-565: a plain unencrypted cookie is trusted for a security decision

CWE-693.name: Protection Mechanism Failure
CWE-693.question: Does it implement, configure or depend on a security protection such as encryption, hashing, random tokens, input filtering, authenticity checks or TLS?

any: cryptographic calls: encryption, hashing, signing, key generation, random number generation
a deny-list, sanitiser or input filter applied as a security control
verification of signatures, origins, checksums, certificates or tokens
storage or transmission of passwords, keys or personal data, or HTTP/cookie security settings
the function only does arithmetic, formatting or data structure work with no security control involved
pure UI layout or rendering code with no security decision

CWE-757.name: Selection of Less-Secure Algorithm During Negotiation ('Algorithm Downgrade')
CWE-757.question: Does this function negotiate a protocol version, cipher or algorithm in a way that lets a peer or attacker push it to a weaker option?

any: the minimum accepted TLS or protocol version is set to an outdated one, or old versions such as SSLv3 and TLS 1.0 are explicitly enabled
the algorithm is chosen from the peer's offered list without filtering out weak entries, or the weakest common choice is picked
after a handshake failure the code retries with a lower version or weaker cipher set
the algorithm name is read from the received message or token header and used as given
only strong versions and ciphers are allowed, with the minimum version set to a current standard
the algorithm is fixed by the code or configuration and the peer cannot influence it
the function uses the library's secure defaults without overriding versions or cipher lists

distinguish_from.CWE-327: a weak algorithm is used directly with no negotiation involved

CWE-759.name: Use of a One-Way Hash without a Salt
CWE-759.question: Does this function hash a password or similar secret with a one-way hash but without any salt?

any: a password is passed straight to a hash call (sha256(password), md5(password)) with nothing else mixed in
the stored digest is compared directly with a hash of the supplied password and no salt is fetched or stored
a random per-user salt is generated and stored alongside the hash
a password hashing library (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2, framework hasher) that salts automatically is used
the input is a high-entropy random token rather than a password

distinguish_from.CWE-760: a salt is used but is predictable or constant
distinguish_from.CWE-916: a salt is present but the hash is too fast

CWE-760.name: Use of a One-Way Hash with a Predictable Salt
CWE-760.question: Does this function salt a password hash with a value that is predictable, constant or reused, such as the username or a fixed string?

any: the salt is a hard-coded literal or global constant
the salt is derived from the username, email, user ID or timestamp
one salt value is shared across all users
the salt comes from a cryptographically secure random generator per password
a password hashing library generates the salt internally

distinguish_from.CWE-759: there is no salt at all

CWE-780.name: Use of RSA Algorithm without OAEP
CWE-780.question: Does this function encrypt with RSA using no padding or old PKCS#1 v1.5 padding instead of OAEP?

any: RSA encryption is performed without OAEP padding
c: RSA_public_encrypt or EVP_PKEY_encrypt with RSA_NO_PADDING or RSA_PKCS1_PADDING
cpp: Crypto++ RSAES_PKCS1v15_Encryptor, or Botan encryption with an EME-PKCS1-v1_5 or raw padding string
javascript: crypto.publicEncrypt with padding set to RSA_PKCS1_PADDING or RSA_NO_PADDING, or a library's raw RSA
python: PKCS1_v1_5 cipher from PyCryptodome or padding.PKCS1v15() used for RSA encryption, or raw pow(m, e, n)
rust: an RSA crate using Pkcs1v15Encrypt or textbook RSA for encryption

any: OAEP padding is specified, such as RSA_PKCS1_OAEP_PADDING, PKCS1_OAEP or padding.OAEP
RSA is used only for signing (where PSS or PKCS#1 v1.5 signature padding applies), not encryption
cpp: Crypto++ RSAES_OAEP_SHA_Encryptor or a Botan OAEP padding such as "OAEP(SHA-256)" is used
javascript: publicEncrypt called with default padding, which is OAEP in Node.js

distinguish_from.CWE-327: a different broken algorithm or mode is in use

CWE-807.name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
CWE-807.question: Does this function make an authentication, authorisation or other security decision from a value the caller can set, such as a cookie, header, hidden field or parameter?

any: a role, isAdmin, authenticated or user id value from a cookie, header, query or form field is tested to grant access
a security check depends on a reverse DNS name, Referer, User-Agent or X-Forwarded-For value
an environment variable or file supplied by an unprivileged user decides whether a privileged action runs
the decision uses server-side state such as a verified session, signed token or database lookup
the untrusted value is protected by a verified signature or MAC before it is used
the value influences only presentation, such as language or layout, not access

distinguish_from.CWE-348: a more trusted source of the same value is available and the code chooses the weaker one
distinguish_from.CWE-565: the untrusted value is specifically a cookie used without validation

CWE-916.name: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-916.question: Does this function hash passwords with a fast hash or too few iterations instead of a deliberately slow password hashing scheme?

any: a password is hashed with a single pass of MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256, salted or not
PBKDF2 or similar is used with a very low iteration count, such as under a few thousand
bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2 with cost parameters reduced to minimal values
passwords are hashed with bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2 or PBKDF2 using a high iteration count
the value hashed is not a password but a high-entropy random token
a framework password hasher with its default work factor is used

distinguish_from.CWE-759: the specific gap is that no salt is used
distinguish_from.CWE-760: the specific gap is that the salt is predictable

CWE-924.name: Improper Enforcement of Message Integrity During Transmission in a Communication Channel
CWE-924.question: Does this function send or receive messages over a connection without any mechanism that detects modification in transit?

any: a socket or network connection exchanges commands or data in plaintext with no MAC, signature or authenticated channel
TLS certificate or hostname verification is disabled for the connection, so an intermediary can alter traffic
encrypted messages use a mode without authentication and the receiver acts on them
the connection uses TLS with certificate verification left on, or another authenticated channel
each message carries a MAC or signature that the receiver verifies before acting
the communication is within the process or over a local pipe not reachable by others

distinguish_from.CWE-295: the only defect shown is disabled or incorrect certificate validation
distinguish_from.CWE-353: the issue is a stored file or record format that lacks an integrity field

CWE-1039.name: Inadequate Detection or Handling of Adversarial Input Perturbations in Automated Recognition Mechanism
CWE-1039.question: Does this function use the output of a machine learning or automated recognition model for a security decision without guarding against misleading inputs?

any: a classifier, face, voice or content-recognition result directly grants access, blocks content or approves a transaction
the top predicted label is used with no confidence threshold, input sanity checks or second factor
raw untrusted images, audio or text go straight into the model with no preprocessing or anomaly check
the model result is one signal combined with other checks, or is reviewed by a person before any security effect
low-confidence or anomalous results are rejected or escalated
the model output has no security consequence, such as tagging photos for search

CWE-1204.name: Generation of Weak Initialization Vector (IV)
CWE-1204.question: Does this function create an initialisation vector or nonce for encryption that is predictable, constant or not unique?

any: the IV is all zeros, a literal, derived from the key or password, or copied from the previous ciphertext block
the IV comes from a counter, timestamp or non-cryptographic random generator
the IV is omitted where the API defaults to a fixed value
the IV is generated per message from a CSPRNG with the cipher's block or nonce size
the crypto library creates the IV internally and returns it with the ciphertext
the function is decrypting with an IV read from the message

distinguish_from.CWE-329: the predictable IV is used specifically with CBC mode
distinguish_from.CWE-323: a nonce is reused across messages with the same key

CWE-1253.name: Incorrect Selection of Fuse Values
CWE-1253.reason: Concerns the logic level chosen for hardware fuses, which is a hardware design property rather than function source code.

CWE-1278.name: Missing Protection Against Hardware Reverse Engineering Using Integrated Circuit (IC) Imaging Techniques
CWE-1278.reason: Concerns physical chip protection against imaging attacks, which no software function can show.

CWE-1291.name: Public Key Re-Use for Signing both Debug and Production Code
CWE-1291.reason: Concerns key management practice for signing builds, a process and deployment matter not visible in one function.

CWE-1293.name: Missing Source Correlation of Multiple Independent Data
CWE-1293.question: Does this function base a security or integrity decision on a single external data source when the code has, or could cheaply consult, an independent second source?

any: a reading, time, location or reputation value from one external source is used for a security decision with no cross-check
several sources are fetched but only the first response is used and the others are ignored
a fallback silently switches to a single source without comparing results
the function compares values from independent sources and rejects or flags disagreement
the value is not security relevant, or comes from a local trusted component
the single source is authenticated and is the only authority by design, such as a signed response from the issuer

distinguish_from.CWE-348: two sources are available and the code picks the less trusted one

CWE-1338.name: Improper Protections Against Hardware Overheating
CWE-1338.reason: Concerns hardware thermal protection features rather than software function code.

CWE-1385.name: Missing Origin Validation in WebSockets
CWE-1385.question: Does this function accept a WebSocket connection or upgrade request without checking the Origin header against an allowed list?

any: a WebSocket upgrade or connection handler accepts the client and starts reading messages with no test of the Origin header
the Origin is read but compared loosely, for example with a substring, startsWith or endsWith test that a hostile domain can satisfy
an origin check option is disabled or set to accept everything, such as a check function that always returns true
the handler compares the Origin header exactly against a fixed allow list and rejects the upgrade otherwise
the connection is authenticated with a per-connection token that is not sent automatically by the browser, such as one passed in the first message
the function is a WebSocket client, or only formats or sends messages on an already accepted connection

distinguish_from.CWE-352: the request is an ordinary HTTP state-changing request without an anti-forgery token, not a WebSocket upgrade

CWE-1428.name: Reliance on HTTP instead of HTTPS
CWE-1428.question: Does this function use or serve plain HTTP for a connection where HTTPS is available and should be used?

any: a hard-coded http:// URL for an API, login, download or update endpoint
a server or redirect configured to listen on or link to http without upgrading to https
a client switches off TLS or follows a downgrade from https to http
the URLs and listeners use https
the http URL is localhost, a loopback test server or an XML namespace identifier that is never fetched
the http listener only redirects to https

distinguish_from.CWE-319: the specific concern is sensitive data being sent unencrypted
